title: Piattos Snow Cheese? Just another hit for URC as sales top P130B
summary: URC's Irwin Lee has had quite a year, with the limited-editied Snow Cheese Piattos selling out, C2 climbing in Vietnam, and Munchy's making its mark in Malaysia

items: Universal Robina Corporation (URC) has launched a new limited-edition snack, Piattos Specials Snow Cheese, which is selling rapidly and may become a permanent product if demand continues.

You can’t have lunch with the head of the country’s biggest snack company without sampling some of those goodies at the table.

And no less than Universal Robina Corporation (URC) president and CEO Irwin Lee was ready to show off his latest product, Piattos Specials Snow Cheese, a limited-edition flavor packaged in a white and blue bag.
Sweet, creamy, and lightly cheesy, the new chips take inspiration from the Korean snack trends that have become popular among younger consumers.
“It’s flying off the shelves,” Lee told reporters on Friday, November 20. “We’re out of stock in a lot of places. We have to make more of it. We’re catching up on supply.”
“‘Pag pumatok ‘yan (If it’s a hit), and if there’s a clamor for it, we’ll make it permanent,” he added.
By then, the bag was empty. After all, it’s not every day you get to share chips with the man in charge of making them.
Of course, there’s much more to URC’s business than this bag of Piattos might betray.
The Gokongwei-led food manufacturer is on track to surpass P175 billion in revenue this year, having already raked in P130.7 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up 5% year-on-year.
One particularly bright spot has been URC’s international business, which now accounts for roughly 20% to 25% of sales.
Take C2, for example. The ready-to-drink tea beloved by Filipinos has apparently won over hearts in Vietnam too, jockeying for the top position against a local brand for the past six months.
“It’s number one in urban Vietnam. And we’re number two in rural,” Lee said, adding that it was the Philippine flavors — lemon and apple in particular — that were topping the charts.
Over in Malaysia, URC’s P24.6-billion acquisition of Munchy’s in 2021 has been “very, very, strong,” according to Lee, solidifying its position as the country’s leading biscuit player.
“We’re running very tight on our biscuit line capacities, so we have to really expand in Malaysia,” he said.

URC expects to maintain its annual capital expenditures of around P6 billion to P8 billion in 2027, with about 15% to 20% allocated to its overseas operations and the biggest chunk of that going to Malaysia.
Back home, however, Filipino consumers have been more cautious.
Lee said inflation has bifurcated growth across categories. Chip sales have slowed down to a low 2% to 3% increase.

Meanwhile, biscuits and bakery products are still enjoying double-digit growth, as are premium drinks like Vitasoy and Blu. And even though chips in general are having a slow year, premium snacks like Calbee potato chips are still selling briskly, with growth in the strong double-digits.
Speaking of treats, URC also has a hand in making Christmas a little sweeter for residents of a certain slice of the metro. And it turns out Lee is quite fond of the man running the place too.
It’s Pasig Mayor Vico Sotto, whose reputation for good governance has earned him admirers well beyond the city.
URC has longstanding ties to Pasig, where founder John Gokongwei Jr. established the company’s predecessor. It still operates flour milling and animal feed facilities there.

Among the goodies that have found their way into Pasig’s annual Christmas giveaway packs are sachets of Swiss Miss hot chocolate, distributed locally by URC. A warm cup of that rich, milky drink with marshmallows is the highlight of many a holiday get-together.

Lee said he had given the Pasig local government a good price for its purchases. But it turns out that the real treat — at least for URC employees — is the job of delivering the goods to city hall. After all, that delivery run might just come with a chance to meet the mayor himself. – Rappler.com
